text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Trade and industry ministry sources say Jordanian firms received United Nations approval for oil-for-food contracts with Iraq worth $68 million so far out of total applications worth $120 million.

- Interior Minister Nazir Rasheed stresses government desire to implement the law and says security forces were carrying out judicial instructions when they destroyed illegal housing in Jordan Valley on Sunday, leading to clashes with residents.

- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali denies existence of Turkish-Israeli plans to empty northern Iraq so they can transfer Palestinians there. Says Jordan will attend Qatar's Middle East economic summit if it is held.
- Flights to restart between Jordan and Kuwait on July 9.
- Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa arriving today for talks with Majali on Egyptian and Jordanian efforts to revive Israeli-Palestinian peace talks.
- Minsterial committee looks into raising cement prices by five percent.
- Ad-Dustour learns that if Moslem Brotherhood decides not to boycott scheduled parliamentary elections, the 11 opposition parties could run for election on a single election list.
- Diplomatic source says Kuwaiti Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad to visit Jordan next month. Government sources say Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati expected in Amman within days.
- Assets of defunct Amman Bank for Investment to be transferred to Arab Bank next month.
- Labour Ministry sources say 87,000 foreign workers who processed their work permits since March paid duties worth five million dinars ($7 million).
- Middle East Investment Bank reports 1996 net profit of 396,000 dinars, says studying options for raising capital to meet Central Bank requirement of 20 million dinars.
- Israeli ambassador to Jordan plays down Ariel Sharon's expected effect on relations.
